papers.title: The mitochondrial theory of sleep: an integrative framework for understanding sleep-wake regulation.
papers.summary: Proposes an integrative mitochondrial theory of sleep, synthesizing disease models, mechanistic data, and bioinformatics gene enrichment analysis. Identifies nine mitochondrial protein-coding genes enriched in oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic, and sleep pathways, and suggests sleep deprivation is linked to calcium signaling, mitochondrial gene expression, ROS, and ATP production, offering a testable model and therapeutic targets such as MCU1, CPT1A, and antioxidant regulators.

papers.title: Chronic joint pain drives sex-specific changes in hippocampal glutamatergic signaling and sleep.
papers.summary: Using a monoiodoacetate knee pain mouse model, this study found sex-specific changes in hippocampal glutamatergic signaling and sleep architecture: both sexes developed mechanical hypersensitivity, but females exhibited poorer sleep outcomes. Injured males showed increased AMPAR-mediated excitatory activity, whereas injured females showed reduced NMDAR activity, and mechanical hypersensitivity correlated with reduced NMDAR/GluN2B function in females and altered AMPAR/NMDAR activity associated with REM sleep.

papers.title: Orexin receptor antagonists attenuate acute stress-induced disruptions in sleep states.
papers.summary: In adult male Sprague Dawley rats exposed to acute inescapable footshock stress, systemic administration of a dual orexin receptor antagonist (suvorexant), an OX1R-preferring antagonist (SB334867), and an OX2R-selective antagonist (EMPA) partially restored REM sleep and attenuated stress-induced increases in NREM sleep. Dual receptor blockade most effectively attenuated NREM increases and reductions in sleep-onset latency, supporting further investigation of DORAs for stress-related sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Multimodal physiological signal learning for clinical sleep respiratory event recognition.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal state-space representation learning framework for automatic recognition of sleep-related breathing events, incorporating dual-branch encoders, cross-state token routing, event query prototype fusion, and class-balanced focal margin loss with auxiliary supervision. On the PSG-Audio public dataset it achieved 88.19% accuracy, 84.51% precision, 86.28% recall, and 92.71% AUROC; on a clinical dataset it achieved 74.33% accuracy, 77.51% precision, 84.33% recall, and 90.51% AUROC.

papers.title: An Investigation of Sleep Macro- and Microarchitecture by APOE Genotype.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis of 3,081 adults aged 50–85 from the Sleep Heart Health Study found that while sleep macroarchitecture was largely comparable across APOE genotypes, micro-level traits differed: ε4 homozygotes had lower spindle power and a dose-response decrease in spindle frequency, and both odds ratio product and arousal index decreased with each ε4 count. These microarchitectural alterations may contribute to Alzheimer's disease risk in ε4 carriers.

papers.title: Exercise timing as a potential temporal regulator of neurolymphatic physiology in neurodegenerative proteinopathies: a mechanistic framework.
papers.summary: This review proposes a mechanistic framework treating exercise timing as a temporal regulator of neurolymphatic clearance in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease, linking timed exercise to glymphatic-meningeal lymphatic function, vascular pulsatility, circadian alignment, and sleep architecture. It argues that timed exercise is a testable biological perturbation rather than a proven disease-modifying treatment and calls for matched-dose trials integrating accelerometry, sleep physiology, circadian measures, vascular assessments, and protein biomarkers.

papers.title: Recent Advances in Research on the Amygdala Complex in Sleep and Anesthesia Awakening: A Hub for the Integration of Emotion and Arousal.
papers.summary: This review proposes that the amygdala complex, comprising lateral, central, and medial nuclei, functions as an 'emotion-arousal integration network' that integrates emotional states with environmental demands to regulate arousal and consciousness. It synthesizes evidence on the basolateral amygdala in sleep-wake cycles, central and medial amygdala in sleep regulation, recovery from general anesthesia, and amygdala dysfunction in PTSD, and discusses clinical translation strategies and research challenges.

papers.title: Locus coeruleus-spinal noradrenergic signaling drives sleep deprivation-induced hyperalgesia via astrocytic GAT-3.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that sleep deprivation activates locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons, increasing spinal norepinephrine that acts on dorsal horn astrocytes via α1-adrenergic receptors to upregulate GAT-3, reduce spinal GABA, and enhance spinoparabrachial neuron activation. Chemogenetic inhibition of spinal-projecting LC noradrenergic neurons reduced astrocytic GAT-3, increased spinal GABA, attenuated acute mechanical hypersensitivity, and shortened incision-evoked mechanical hypersensitivity.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machines and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states from resting-state EEG using spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity features encoded into quantum states. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved accuracies of 96.88% at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Mating imperatives drive plasticity of the daily temporal niche in fruit flies.
papers.summary: By monitoring daily activity of twilight-active Drosophila species under naturalistic conditions, the study shows that intense sociosexual interactions rapidly reformat their crepuscular niche: chemosensory reliance shifts activity into the night while visual reliance shifts it into the day. This temporal plasticity bypasses the circadian clock and operates via a conserved dopaminergic pathway that inhibits sleep and sustains sexual motivation, driving niche divergence that may facilitate sympatric coexistence.

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Electroencephalography Predicts Acute Cerebral Injury in the Pediatric ICU.
papers.summary: A prospective study applied machine learning to clinical and EEG features to predict acute cerebral injury in pediatric ICU patients. The SVM with RBF kernel achieved the highest accuracy (AUROC 0.95, test accuracy 0.90) for binary classification, while logistic regression performed best for multiclass classification (accuracy 0.77).

papers.title: Reassessing Global Field Synchronization as a Phase-Synchrony EEG Metric: Mathematical Review and Empirical Counterexamples With Implications for Wearable Pain Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper re-evaluates Global Field Synchronization (GFS) as a phase-synchrony EEG metric using mathematical review, synthetic simulations, and empirical resting-state EEG. It found that GFS can dissociate from true phase dispersion (circular standard deviation) under rotations and scaling, and that the expected inverse GFS-CSD relationship was not consistently observed across EEG frequency bands, indicating GFS is not a valid proxy for EEG phase synchronization and limiting its use as a wearable connectivity biomarker.

papers.title: Sleep electroencephalography-derived brain health and long-term cognitive decline in community-dwelling adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: In 639 community-dwelling adults, higher sleep EEG-derived Brain Health Score (BHS) was associated with slower cognitive decline in memory, executive function, and language over an average of 14.3 years. Brain Age Index (BAI) showed no association with cognitive decline.

papers.title: Melatonin beyond chronobiology: integrating pharmacokinetics, dose-exposure forecasting, and clinical evidence.
papers.summary: This review integrates preclinical and clinical evidence with pharmacokinetic data and ODE-based dose-exposure modeling to evaluate whether non-circadian effects of melatonin can be interpreted within an exposure-based pharmacological framework. It finds that clinical evidence is most coherent for sleep and circadian outcomes, while evidence for other applications is heterogeneous and often lacks pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic measurements.

papers.title: Pkd1 Deficiency Causes Intrinsic Renal Circadian Clock Dysfunction.
papers.summary: Using slow and rapidly progressing ADPKD mouse models and Pkd1-deficient renal epithelial cells, this study examined whether Pkd1 loss causes intrinsic renal circadian clock dysfunction. It reports that Pkd1 deficiency dampens and desynchronizes core clock gene oscillations and PER2::LUC bioluminescence in kidneys and cells, indicating cell-autonomous circadian clock dysfunction independent of systemic cues.

papers.title: Pharmacological modulation of hyperarousal in insomnia associated with major depressive disorder: a narrative review of sedating antidepressants and orexin receptor antagonists.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how heterogeneous insomnia presentations in major depressive disorder may inform the use of sedating antidepressants and dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs). It proposes a hypothesis-generating framework, noting that DORAs have the strongest evidence for insomnia disorder, particularly sleep maintenance, but evidence in active MDD remains limited.

papers.title: The impact of obstructive sleep apnea on skin wound healing - from preclinical perspective to clinical evidence: A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates cellular mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and clinical data to propose that obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) may impair skin wound healing indirectly through comorbidities and directly via intermittent hypoxia (IH). It reports that IH delays wound closure, downregulates HIF-2α and VEGF, shifts macrophages pro-inflammatory, and that high OSA risk doubled poor healing risk in diabetic foot ulcers.

papers.title: Chronobiology of fracture repair: local molecular clocks, rhythm protection, and time-anchored translation.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on circadian regulation of fracture repair, noting that local molecular clocks operate in the fracture niche and that perioperative disruptions may affect healing. It advocates for a time-anchored research framework but concludes that current evidence does not support specific clinical chronotherapy recommendations.

papers.title: Melatonin receptor 1 signaling modulates the metabolic response to high-fat diet in female melatonin-proficient mice.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of low-fat and high-fat diets on liver biology and transcriptome in melatonin-proficient female mice with MT1 knockout. It found that MT1 deletion alone caused no notable metabolic changes, but combined with high-fat diet led to significant alterations in glucose tolerance, serum lipids, hepatic lipid accumulation, and liver transcriptome, potentially linked to estrogen-related pathways.

papers.title: Pancreatic Cancer Disrupts Circadian Patterns of Gene Expression in Cardiorespiratory Muscles.
papers.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
papers.summary: In an orthotopic KPC pancreatic cancer cachexia model, circadian transcriptomes of diaphragm and heart showed that ~60% of rhythmic genes lost rhythmicity in both tissues, with diaphragm disruptions in core clock and metabolic networks and heart loss of rhythmicity in beta-adrenergic/cAMP and insulin response networks, while inflammatory networks gained rest-phase rhythmicity. These findings indicate widespread circadian dysregulation in cardiorespiratory muscles during cachexia.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations in Anhedonia Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder and Their Modulation by Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation.
papers.summary: In 50 MDD patients stratified by anhedonia severity, iTBS modulated EEG microstate dynamics differently: low-anhedonia patients showed normalization of most microstate parameters, while high-anhedonia patients had persistent abnormalities. In high-anhedonia patients, clinical improvement correlated with microstate changes, suggesting microstates as treatment response markers.

papers.title: Adrenergic Pathways Mediate Circadian IOP Rhythm in Rats.
papers.summary: This study used wireless telemetry to monitor intraocular pressure (IOP) in rats and applied adrenergic receptor agonists and antagonists to identify mechanisms underlying circadian IOP rhythm. It found that β-, α1-, and α2-adrenergic pathways are all necessary to elevate IOP during subjective night, while β- and α1-receptor activation is sufficient to raise daytime IOP to nighttime levels.

papers.title: Management of Non-REM parasomnias: A systematic review of evidence-based treatment approaches.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 14 mostly retrospective uncontrolled studies evaluated treatments for NREM parasomnias, finding that pharmacotherapy (especially benzodiazepines) and cognitive behavioral therapy were the most studied interventions; most suggested benefit but certainty was very low and heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. High-quality trials with standardized objective measurements are needed.

papers.title: Sleep disorders in stroke rehabilitation: mechanisms, impacts, and multidisciplinary management - a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes the bidirectional relationship between sleep disorders and stroke, reporting that OSA increases stroke risk approximately 2- to 3-fold and post-stroke sleep disorders affect up to 59.9% of patients, with mechanisms including intermittent hypoxia, inflammation, and autonomic dysregulation. CPAP, CBT-I, and rTMS are highlighted as evidence-based management strategies, though high-quality RCTs are needed.

papers.title: Cryptochrome-mediated integration of circadian rhythms into seasonal cycles in the silkworm Bombyx mori.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent genome-editing evidence on silkworm cryptochromes BmCRY1 and BmCRY2, showing that Bmcry1 loss disrupts hatching and eclosion rhythms and impairs photoperiodic diapause modulation while temperature-dependent diapause under constant darkness is retained, whereas Bmcry2 mutants show reduced temperature-dependent diapause induction. The findings position cryptochromes at the interface of circadian timing and seasonal developmental control.

papers.title: [Sleep disorders associated with montelukast in children with respiratory allergy].
papers.journal: Revista medica del Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 120 children with asthma and/or allergic rhinitis, montelukast users had a significantly higher prevalence of sleep disorders (73.02%) compared to non-users (14.17%), with an odds ratio of 8.31 (p < 0.0001). The study concludes that montelukast use was associated with sleep disorders in this pediatric population.

papers.title: Digital distraction and adolescent development: a narrative review of smartphone use, cognitive effects, and policy interventions.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on adolescent smartphone use and its effects on psychological well-being, cognitive functioning, and school policy responses. It reports that excessive smartphone use is consistently but modestly associated with sleep disruption, reduced attentional capacity, and increased internalizing symptoms, with heterogeneous effects moderated by activity type, timing, and individual vulnerability; school phone bans improve classroom attention and engagement but broader mental health impacts remain unclear.

papers.title: Hypoxic burden reduction after lateral pharyngoplasty in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: Beyond the apnea-hypopnea index.
papers.summary: This longitudinal observational study evaluated changes in hypoxic burden after lateral pharyngoplasty in 27 adults with obstructive sleep apnea. It found significant reductions in hypoxic burden across all sleep states and positions, including among patients classified as surgical failures by Sher's criteria, suggesting hypoxic burden is a more sensitive metric than the apnea-hypopnea index alone.

papers.title: Application of Circadian Rhythm-Based Pulmonary Rehabilitation in Patients with Severe Pneumonia-A Feasibility Study With Convenience Sampling.
papers.journal: Archives of rehabilitation research and clinical translation
papers.summary: This feasibility study with convenience sampling assigned 93 severe pneumonia patients to routine pulmonary rehabilitation or a circadian rhythm-based comprehensive program. The intervention group had significantly shorter mechanical ventilation and hospital stay, higher rehabilitation compliance, better pulmonary function and sleep quality, and greater nursing satisfaction.

papers.title: Regulating the Hyperdopaminergic Substrate in Restless Legs Syndrome With Augmentation: An Open-label Study on the Safety and Efficacy of Aripiprazole.
papers.summary: This open-label observational study tested low-dose aripiprazole (5 mg daily) with gradual dopamine agonist tapering in 18 adults with severe restless legs syndrome and augmentation. All patients discontinued dopamine agonists, with significant improvements in IRLS scores, CGI, subjective sleep time, and sleep quality, and only mild transient adverse events.

papers.title: Multi-modal connectome analysis of the stereoelectroencephalography implantation effect: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report used longitudinal multi-modal connectome analysis in a patient with drug-resistant right temporal lobe epilepsy who experienced seizure reduction after stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) implantation. The findings showed decreased hippocampus-amygdala and fusiform gyrus-temporal pole connectivity, increased hippocampus-posterior cingulate connectivity, reduced connectome eccentricity, and histopathological evidence of lymphocytic infiltration and reactive gliosis around electrode trajectories.

papers.title: Cloning of a novel cyanobacterial serotonin N-acetyltransferase gene CySNAT3 and its integration with transcriptomic drug repurposing in pediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing.
papers.summary: The study cloned, expressed, and purified a novel cyanobacterial serotonin N-acetyltransferase (CySNAT3) that catalyzes melatonin synthesis, and integrated transcriptomic drug repurposing of pediatric oSDB tonsillar RNA-seq data to identify four candidate drugs with favorable binding to target proteins.

papers.title: Association of Circadian Syndrome with Incident Risk of 23 Site-Specific Cancers: A Large-Scale Prospective Study in the UK Biobank.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study in 367,832 UK Biobank participants examined associations between circadian syndrome (combining metabolic, sleep, and mood traits) and incident cancer risk. Circadian syndrome was associated with higher overall cancer incidence and the strongest positive associations were for endometrial, liver, and kidney cancers; sex-hormone-binding globulin accounted for 51.0% of the endometrial cancer association and C-reactive protein for 26.4% of the overall cancer association.

papers.title: Individualized perioperative nutritional management in orthognathic surgery: an evidence-graded, integrated framework linking upper-airway change, feeding function, and psychological status.
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes evidence on perioperative nutritional management in orthognathic surgery, grading three domains (upper-airway change, feeding function, psychological status) by proximity to nutritional outcomes, and proposes a hypothesis-generating risk-stratified framework highlighting that only feeding function has direct longitudinal support.

papers.title: A rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication with tetrasomy (CN=4) and adjacent trisomy (CN=3) associated with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: A case report describes a Chinese girl with a rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication comprising a tetrasomic and adjacent trisomic segment, presenting with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges, expanding the genomic spectrum of complex proximal 15q rearrangements.

papers.title: Sleep duration inversely correlates with glucolipid metabolism in patients with new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.summary: In 168 patients with new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus, sleep duration was inversely correlated with glucolipid metabolism indices and abdominal total fat area, and positively correlated with good glycemic control. Short sleep duration, along with high BMI, FBG, TG, and TFA, was identified as an independent contributor to poor glycemic control.

papers.title: The circadian clock protein CmLHY integrates strigolactone signaling to regulate short-day-induced flowering in chrysanthemum.
papers.summary: The study identifies a strigolactone signaling complex (CmMAX2-CmD14.1-CmD53) that regulates short-day-induced flowering in chrysanthemum, showing that CmD53 represses the florigen gene CmFTL3 and that the circadian clock protein CmLHY integrates strigolactone signaling by repressing CmMAX2 and CmD14.1, with conservation in rice.

papers.title: Effectiveness of medical clowning in reducing postoperative pain and improving sleep quality in school-aged children.
papers.summary: A quasi-experimental study found that a single medical clowning session significantly reduced postoperative pain at 30 and 60 minutes and improved sleep quality in school-aged children compared to routine care.

papers.title: The Global Initiative for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (GIFOSA): Rationale, Strategic Framework, and Call to Action.
papers.summary: This paper presents the rationale and strategic framework of the Global Initiative for Obstructive Sleep Apnea (GIFOSA), an implementation-focused initiative to address global disparities in obstructive sleep apnea care through coordinated clinical, workforce, person-centered, and policy pillars.

papers.title: Mental Health of Early and Prolonged Parent-Child Separated Children in Chinese Immigrant Families: A Qualitative Study With Parent-Child Dyads.
papers.summary: A qualitative interview study with 24 parent-child dyads from Chinese immigrant families examined mental health in children who experienced early and prolonged separation as "satellite babies" sent to China and later reunited with parents. The study reported both negative outcomes (avoidance of disclosure, social withdrawal, externalized and internalized problems, low-quality sleep) and positive mental health conditions (positive general mental health perception, high self-esteem, healthy social engagement, high-quality sleep), indicating within-group mental health disparities.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
